text: After six days, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain by themselves.
label: Matthew 17:1

text: He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his garments became as white as the light.
label: Matthew 17:2

text: Behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them talking with him.
label: Matthew 17:3

text: Peter answered, and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, let’s make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
label: Matthew 17:4

text: While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. Behold, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.”
label: Matthew 17:5

text: When the disciples heard it, they fell on their faces, and were very afraid.
label: Matthew 17:6

text: Jesus came and touched them and said, “Get up, and don’t be afraid.”
label: Matthew 17:7

text: Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, except Jesus alone.
label: Matthew 17:8

text: As they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, “Don’t tell anyone what you saw, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”
label: Matthew 17:9

text: His disciples asked him, saying, “Then why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
label: Matthew 17:10

text: Jesus answered them, “Elijah indeed comes first, and will restore all things,
label: Matthew 17:11

text: but I tell you that Elijah has come already, and they didn’t recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted to. Even so the Son of Man will also suffer by them.”
label: Matthew 17:12

text: Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them of John the Baptizer.
label: Matthew 17:13

text: When they came to the multitude, a man came to him, kneeling down to him, and saying,
label: Matthew 17:14

text: “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is epileptic, and suffers grievously; for he often falls into the fire, and often into the water.
label: Matthew 17:15

text: So I brought him to your disciples, and they could not cure him.”
label: Matthew 17:16

text: Jesus answered, “Faithless and perverse generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him here to me.”
label: Matthew 17:17

text: Jesus rebuked him, the demon went out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour.
label: Matthew 17:18

text: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately, and said, “Why weren’t we able to cast it out?”
label: Matthew 17:19

text: He said to them, “Because of your unbelief. For most certainly I tell you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
label: Matthew 17:20

text: But this kind doesn’t go out except by prayer and fasting.”
label: Matthew 17:21

variants.reading: the verse is absent (the saying ends at v 20, without the 'prayer and fasting' clause)
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Matthew' records for Matthew 17:21 'verse omitted' in aleph* (Sinaiticus), B (Vaticanus), Theta, 0281 and further Greek manuscripts, the Latin, Syriac, Coptic, Ethiopic and Georgian versions and Eusebius. The WEB prints the verse; this graph carries the omission as the variant.

text: While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men,
label: Matthew 17:22

text: and they will kill him, and the third day he will be raised up.” They were exceedingly sorry.
label: Matthew 17:23

text: When they had come to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma coins came to Peter, and said, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the didrachma?”
label: Matthew 17:24

text: He said, “Yes.” When he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute? From their children, or from strangers?”
label: Matthew 17:25

text: Peter said to him, “From strangers.” Jesus said to him, “Therefore the children are exempt.
label: Matthew 17:26

text: But, lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater coin. Take that, and give it to them for me and you.”
label: Matthew 17:27

excerpt: The Second Temple served as the chief place of worship, ritual sacrifice (korban), and communal gathering for the Jewish people, among whom it regularly attracted pilgrims for the Three Pilgrimage Festivals: Passover, Shavuot, and Sukkot.

label: Transfiguration on a high mountain
statement: After six days Jesus took Peter, James and John up a high mountain and was transfigured before them. The mountain is not named; since the 3rd century tradition has identified it with Mount Tabor, while others argue for a ridge near Caesarea Philippi, usually Mount Hermon.
note: Disputed identification (grade D for any): Tabor (Origen and later tradition, against the fortress objection) versus Hermon or 'some mountain near Caesarea-Philippi' (Lightfoot; France 1987).

label: Moses and Elijah appear with Jesus
statement: Moses and Elijah appeared and talked with Jesus at the transfiguration - the Law and the Prophets with the Son.

label: Peter's three tents (sukkot)
statement: Peter proposed making three tents (skênai, booths) - one for Jesus, one for Moses, one for Elijah - the language of the sukkot dwelt in at the Feast of Tabernacles.

label: Elijah must come first
statement: The scribes taught that Elijah must come first before the restoration; Jesus answered that Elijah has already come, and the disciples understood that he spoke of John the Baptist (reusing the Elijah-expectation node from ch 11).

label: The 'moonstruck' (epileptic) boy
statement: A boy was brought with epilepsy - Greek selêniazetai, 'moonstruck' - the condition Greek medicine called the 'sacred disease' and antiquity linked with the moon.
note: The moon-seizure association is ancient (a Babylonian sufferer was 'diagnosed as being under the influence of a moon god'); the Wikipedia source documenting it is modern documentation, not evidence.

label: Faith as a grain of mustard seed
statement: Jesus likened faith to a grain of mustard seed - proverbially tiny - which could tell 'this mountain' to move; reusing the ch 13 mustard nodes.

label: The second passion prediction, in Galilee
statement: While staying in Galilee Jesus predicted that the Son of Man would be delivered into the hands of men, killed, and raised the third day.

label: The didrachma collectors and the half-shekel Temple tax
statement: At Capernaum collectors of the didrachma asked whether Jesus paid it - the annual half-shekel Temple tax for the upkeep of the Temple (Exod 30:13).

label: Kings take toll and poll-tax from strangers
statement: The kings of the earth take toll (telos) and poll-tax (kênsos) from strangers, not from their own children - the imperial taxation of subject peoples.

label: The stater in the fish's mouth
statement: Peter was to find a stater in the mouth of the first fish he hooked - a coin of four drachmae, two didrachmas - paying the tax 'for me and you'.
